_note: Absorbability of query-side transforms into a freely-parameterised vocab x dim table under normalize(weighted mean of rows). ABSORBABLE means the transform adds NO capacity a trained table lacks -- it can still help as a prior/initialisation, but it cannot raise the architecture's ceiling. This CORRECTS research/m7-research-2026-08-26.md, which classed query-side centering and top-PC removal as 'genuine new capacity'. They are not: mean_t(W_t - mu) = mean_t(W_t) - mu exactly, for every token multiset.

setup.queries: ragged multisets with repeats and a shared prefix token

centering: normalize(mean - mu).reconstruction: W' = W - mu (subtract mu from EVERY row)

per-token weights: normalize(sum c_t W_t.reconstruction: W' = c_t * W_t (scale each row by its own weight)

count saturation (unique-tokens-only).reconstruction: IMPOSSIBLE: the correction depends on each query's multiplicity vector, and a row is shared across all queries

length scaling (1/sqrt|T| instead of 1/|.reconstruction: VACUOUS: any positive scalar function of |T| is removed by the final L2 normalization, so it is a no-op, not a lever

n-gram / phrase rows.reconstruction: NOT absorbable: two queries with the same token multiset in a different order get IDENTICAL unigram-bag vectors, so no choice of unigram rows can separate them. An n-gram row can.

consequence: Of the levers in the plan, only n-gram/phrase rows and multiplicity-dependent pooling (count saturation) add capacity. Centering, whitening, top-PC removal, IDF and SIF weighting are all re-parameterisations -- and per-token weighting is ALREADY in the architecture (QueryTable.learned_weights), so p1-objB could in principle have learned the SIF weighting itself.
